source.text: לַמְנַצֵּ֥חַ עַֽל־יְדוּת֗וּן לְאָסָ֥ף מִזְמֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: For the director, on Jeduthun. Of Asaph, a psalm.

en.L: For the director: on Jeduthun. Of Asaph, a psalm.
en.B: For the music director. On Jeduthun. A psalm of Asaph.
en.R: For the leader of the music. For Jeduthun. A song of Asaph.

fr.L: Au chef de chœur : sur Jeduthun. D’Asaph, psaume.
fr.B: Au chef de chœur. Sur Jeduthun. Psaume d’Asaph.
fr.R: Pour le chef des musiciens. Pour Jeduthun. Chant d’Asaph.

sw.L: Kwa kiongozi wa kwaya: kwa Yeduthuni. Ya Asafu, zaburi.
sw.B: Kwa kiongozi wa kwaya. Kwa Yeduthuni. Zaburi ya Asafu.
sw.R: Kwa kiongozi wa waimbaji. Kwa Yeduthuni. Wimbo wa Asafu.

decisions.choice: The title is verse 1
decisions.reason: The title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: the director: the one who leads the music
decisions.reason: As in 4:1, probably the leader of the temple music.

decisions.choice: on Jeduthun: in the manner of Jeduthun's singers
decisions.reason: Jeduthun was one of the leaders of the music at the sanctuary in David's time (1 Chronicles 16:41; 25:1). Psalm 39 is "for Jeduthun"; here and in Psalm 62 the word is "on", which may mean the psalm was sung in the style or by the choir that bore his name.

decisions.choice: Jeduthun: the name as read, not as written
decisions.reason: As in 39:1, the Hebrew writes the name with a slightly different spelling and its notes say to read it as Jeduthun. The words follow the form to be read.

decisions.choice: Asaph: a leader of the temple singers
decisions.reason: Asaph was a Levite whom David appointed to lead the singing before the ark (1 Chronicles 16:5-7); his family carried on the work (1 Chronicles 25:1-2). Psalms 50 and 73-83 bear his name.

decisions.choice: song
decisions.reason: As in 3:1, Readable says what a psalm is.

decisions.choice: "Jeduthun", the established French spelling of the name
decisions.reason: Jeduthun was one of David's chief musicians (meaning decision m3). French Bibles have long written his name "Jeduthun"; a transcription such as "Yedoutoun" would be closer to the Hebrew sounds but less familiar.

source.text: קוֹלִ֣י אֶל־אֱלֹהִ֣ים וְאֶצְעָ֑קָה קוֹלִ֥י אֶל־אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים וְהַאֲזִ֥ין אֵלָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: My voice to God, and I will cry out; my voice to God, and he will give ear to me.

en.L: My voice [goes] to God, and I cry out; \q my voice [goes] to God, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will give ear to me.
en.B: I raise my voice to God and cry out; \q I raise my voice to God, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will listen to me.
en.R: I call out loud to God for help. \q I call out loud to God, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will hear me.

fr.L: Ma voix [va] vers Dieu, et je crie ; \q ma voix [va] vers Dieu, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} me prêtera l’oreille.
fr.B: J’élève la voix vers Dieu et je crie ; \q j’élève la voix vers Dieu, pour qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} m’écoute.
fr.R: J’appelle Dieu à grands cris pour qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} m’aide. \q J’appelle Dieu à grands cris, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} m’entendra.

sw.L: Sauti yangu [inamwendea] Mungu, nami ninalia; \q sauti yangu [inamwendea] Mungu, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} atanitegea sikio.
sw.B: Ninapaza sauti yangu kwa Mungu na kulia; \q ninapaza sauti yangu kwa Mungu, ili {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} anisikilize.
sw.R: Ninamwita Mungu kwa sauti kubwa anisaidie. \q Ninamwita Mungu kwa sauti kubwa, naye {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} atanisikia.

decisions.choice: and he will give ear: so that he may listen
alternatives: and he gave ear to me
decisions.reason: The verb form (ha'azin with "and") usually looks ahead: the cry is raised so that God will hear. The psalm then tells of a long night in which he seemed silent (verses 3-10).

decisions.choice: God: the name used in Psalms 42-83
decisions.reason: Like the other psalms of Asaph, this psalm mostly says "God" ('Elohim), and uses the short form of the divine name only once (verse 12).

decisions.choice: I raise my voice (B); I call out loud (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the short Hebrew phrase "my voice to God" into a full sentence.

source.text: בְּי֥וֹם צָרָתִי֮ אֲדֹנָ֪י דָּ֫רָ֥שְׁתִּי יָדִ֤י׀לַ֣יְלָה נִ֭גְּרָה וְלֹ֣א תָפ֑וּג מֵאֲנָ֖ה הִנָּחֵ֣ם נַפְשִֽׁי׃

records.literal_gloss: In [the] day of my distress [the] Lord I sought; my hand [by] night was stretched out and did not grow numb; refused to be comforted my soul.

en.L: In the day of my distress I sought [the] Lord; \q at night my hand was stretched out and did not grow numb; \q my soul refused to be comforted.
en.B: When trouble came I looked for the Lord; \q all night I kept my hands raised and did not tire, \q and I would take no comfort.
en.R: When I was in trouble, I went to the Lord for help. \q All night long I held up my hands to pray and did not stop. \q Nothing anyone said could comfort me.

fr.L: Au jour de ma détresse, j’ai cherché [le] Seigneur ; \q la nuit, ma main s’est tendue et ne s’est pas engourdie ; \q mon âme a refusé d’être consolée.
fr.B: Quand la détresse est venue, j’ai cherché le Seigneur ; \q toute la nuit j’ai gardé les mains levées sans me lasser, \q et je refusais toute consolation.
fr.R: Quand j’étais dans le malheur, je suis allé vers le Seigneur pour qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} m’aide. \q Toute la nuit, j’ai levé les mains pour prier, sans m’arrêter. \q Rien de ce qu’on me disait ne pouvait me consoler.

sw.L: Katika siku ya taabu yangu nilimtafuta Bwana; \q usiku mkono wangu ulinyooshwa wala haukulegea; \q nafsi yangu ilikataa kufarijiwa.
sw.B: Taabu ilipokuja nilimtafuta Bwana; \q usiku kucha niliinua mikono yangu bila kuchoka, \q wala sikukubali kufarijiwa.
sw.R: Nilipokuwa katika taabu, nilimwendea Bwana nipate msaada. \q Usiku kucha niliinua mikono yangu kuomba wala sikuacha. \q Hakuna neno la mtu yeyote lililoweza kunifariji.

decisions.choice: my hand stretched out: lifted in prayer
decisions.reason: Spreading out the hands toward God is the posture of prayer (Exodus 9:29; 143:6). The psalmist prayed all night without letting his hands drop.

decisions.choice: was stretched out and did not grow numb
alternatives: my hand (my wound) ran and did not stop
decisions.reason: The verb (nagar) means to pour out or flow, and is used of eyes streaming with tears (Lamentations 3:49). With "hand" it is taken as stretched out in prayer; it may instead picture a sore that kept running.

decisions.choice: refused to be comforted: like Jacob mourning Joseph
decisions.reason: The same words are used of Jacob, who refused to be comforted when he thought Joseph was dead (Genesis 37:35).

decisions.choice: I
decisions.reason: As in Psalms 1-12, nefesh is "soul" at Literal and the whole person at Balanced and Readable.

source.text: אֶזְכְּרָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֣ים וְאֶֽהֱמָיָ֑ה אָשִׂ֓יחָה׀וְתִתְעַטֵּ֖ף רוּחִ֣י סֶֽלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: I remember God, and I moan; I muse, and faints my spirit. Selah.

en.L: I remember God, and I moan; \q I muse, and my spirit faints. Selah
en.B: I think of God and groan; \q I ponder, and my spirit sinks. Selah
en.R: When I think about God, I groan. \q The more I think, the weaker I feel. Selah

fr.L: Je me souviens de Dieu, et je gémis ; \q je médite, et mon esprit défaille. Sélah
fr.B: Je pense à Dieu et je soupire ; \q je réfléchis, et mon esprit s’affaisse. Sélah
fr.R: Quand je pense à Dieu, je gémis. \q Plus je réfléchis, plus je me sens faible. Sélah

sw.L: Namkumbuka Mungu, nami ninaugua; \q ninatafakari, na roho yangu inazimia. Sela
sw.B: Ninamfikiri Mungu na kuugua; \q ninawaza, na roho yangu inafifia. Sela
sw.R: Ninapomfikiri Mungu, ninaugua. \q Kadiri ninavyowaza, ndivyo ninavyozidi kudhoofika. Sela

decisions.choice: I remember God, and I moan: memory brings pain
alternatives: when I remember God I moan
decisions.reason: Remembering God at first brings no comfort, because the God who once acted seems far away now. Later in the psalm the same verb (zakar, verses 7 and 12) leads to hope.

decisions.choice: muse: turn over in the mind, or complain
decisions.reason: The verb (siach) means to think something over, often aloud, and can mean to pour out a complaint (55:3; 142:3).

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

source.text: אָ֭חַזְתָּ שְׁמֻר֣וֹת עֵינָ֑י נִ֝פְעַ֗מְתִּי וְלֹ֣א אֲדַבֵּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: You held [the] guards of my eyes; I was troubled and did not speak.

en.L: You held [open] the guards of my eyes; \q I was troubled and could not speak.
en.B: You would not let my eyelids close; \q I was too shaken to say a word.
en.R: You kept me awake all night. \q I was so upset that I could not even speak.

fr.L: Tu as tenu [ouvertes] les gardes de mes yeux ; \q j’étais troublé et je ne pouvais parler.
fr.B: Tu empêchais mes paupières de se fermer ; \q j’étais trop bouleversé pour dire un mot.
fr.R: Tu m’as empêché de dormir toute la nuit. \q J’étais si agité que je ne pouvais même pas parler.

sw.L: Wewe uliishika [wazi] kope za macho yangu; \q nilifadhaika wala sikuweza kusema.
sw.B: Hukuniacha nifumbe kope zangu; \q nilitikiswa mno nisiweze kusema neno.
sw.R: Ulinifanya nikeshe usiku kucha. \q Nilihuzunika sana hata sikuweza kusema.

decisions.choice: the guards of my eyes: my eyelids
alternatives: the night watches of my eyes
decisions.reason: The word (shemurot) means guards or watches. Here it is taken as the eyelids that guard the eyes, which God held open; it may also mean the watches of the night (63:7; 119:148), which God kept the psalmist awake through.

decisions.choice: you held: God is behind the sleeplessness
decisions.reason: The psalmist turns to God and sees even his sleepless night as in God's hands.

decisions.choice: You kept me awake all night
alternatives: You held the guards of my eyes
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means (m1).

source.text: חִשַּׁ֣בְתִּי יָמִ֣ים מִקֶּ֑דֶם שְׁ֝נ֗וֹת עוֹלָמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: I thought about days from antiquity, years of ages.

en.L: I thought about the days of old, \q the years of ages past.
en.B: I turned my mind to days gone by, \q to years long past.
en.R: I thought about the past, \q about what happened long ago.

fr.L: J’ai pensé aux jours d’autrefois, \q aux années des âges passés.
fr.B: J’ai tourné mes pensées vers les jours d’autrefois, \q vers les années lointaines.
fr.R: J’ai pensé au passé, \q à ce qui s’est passé il y a très longtemps.

sw.L: Nilizifikiri siku za kale, \q miaka ya zamani za kale.
sw.B: Niliyaelekeza mawazo yangu kwa siku zilizopita, \q kwa miaka iliyopita zamani.
sw.R: Niliwaza juu ya wakati uliopita, \q juu ya mambo yaliyotokea zamani.

decisions.choice: days of old: the time of God's great acts
decisions.reason: The days "from of old" (qedem) are the early days of Israel, above all the rescue from Egypt that the psalm will recall in verses 16-21 (44:2; 143:5).

source.text: אֶֽזְכְּרָ֥ה נְגִינָתִ֗י בַּ֫לָּ֥יְלָה עִם־לְבָבִ֥י אָשִׂ֑יחָה וַיְחַפֵּ֥שׂ רוּחִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: I remember my song in the night; with my heart I muse, and searched my spirit:

en.L: I remember my song in the night; \q I muse with my heart, \q and my spirit searched:
en.B: I call to mind the songs I sang at night; \q I talk with my own heart, \q and my spirit searches for answers:
en.R: At night I remember the songs I used to sing. \q I think hard, \q and deep inside I keep asking:

fr.L: Je me souviens de mon chant dans la nuit ; \q je médite avec mon cœur, \q et mon esprit a cherché :
fr.B: Je me rappelle les chants que je chantais la nuit ; \q je m’entretiens avec mon propre cœur, \q et mon esprit cherche des réponses :
fr.R: La nuit, je me souviens des chants que je chantais autrefois. \q Je réfléchis beaucoup, \q et au fond de moi, je me demande sans cesse :

sw.L: Nakumbuka wimbo wangu usiku; \q natafakari kwa moyo wangu, \q na roho yangu ilichunguza:
sw.B: Nazikumbuka nyimbo nilizoimba usiku; \q nazungumza na moyo wangu mwenyewe, \q na roho yangu inatafuta majibu:
sw.R: Usiku nazikumbuka nyimbo nilizokuwa nikiimba. \q Nafikiri sana, \q na ndani yangu ninaendelea kuuliza:

decisions.choice: my song: music I once played and sang
decisions.reason: The word (neginah) is a song played on strings (as in the title of Psalm 76). The psalmist remembers the songs of better days, perhaps songs in the night like those of 42:9.

decisions.choice: my spirit searched: the questions that follow
decisions.reason: The searching of his spirit is put into words in the questions of verses 8-10, so this verse ends with a colon.

decisions.choice: the songs I used to sing
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that the songs belong to an earlier, happier time (m1).

source.text: הַֽ֭לְעוֹלָמִים יִזְנַ֥ח׀אֲדֹנָ֑י וְלֹֽא־יֹסִ֖יף לִרְצ֣וֹת עֽוֹד׃

records.literal_gloss: Forever will reject [the] Lord, and not will he again be favorable anymore?

en.L: Will [the] Lord reject forever, \q and will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} never again show favor?
en.B: Will the Lord turn away for all time, \q and never again show kindness?
en.R: Will the Lord turn away from us forever? \q Will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} never be kind to us again?

fr.L: Le Seigneur rejettera-t-il pour toujours, \q et ne montrera-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} plus jamais {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} faveur ?
fr.B: Le Seigneur va-t-il se détourner pour toujours, \q et ne plus jamais montrer {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} bonté ?
fr.R: Le Seigneur va-t-il se détourner de nous pour toujours ? \q Ne sera-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} plus jamais bon pour nous ?

sw.L: Je, Bwana atakataa milele, \q wala hataonyesha tena kibali?
sw.B: Je, Bwana atageuka mbali siku zote, \q wala hataonyesha wema tena kamwe?
sw.R: Je, Bwana atatuacha milele? \q Je, hatatuonea wema tena kamwe?

decisions.choice: reject: cast off, turn away from
decisions.reason: The verb (zanach) is used for God casting off his people in the laments of this collection (44:10; 74:1).

decisions.choice: questions that hope for the answer no
decisions.reason: The questions of verses 8-10 voice the psalmist's fear, but each also implies that it cannot be so: God's loyal love and promises do not end.

decisions.choice: us
decisions.reason: Readable supplies the object the Hebrew leaves unsaid: God's people.

source.text: הֶאָפֵ֣ס לָנֶ֣צַח חַסְדּ֑וֹ גָּ֥מַר אֹ֝֗מֶר לְדֹ֣ר וָדֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: Has ceased to perpetuity his loyal love? Has come to an end [the] word for generation and generation?

en.L: Has {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love ceased forever? \q Has [{{deity_pronoun:his|His}}] word come to an end for generation after generation?
en.B: Is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love gone for good? \q Is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} promise finished for every generation to come?
en.R: Has {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithful love ended for good? \q Are {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} promises over for all time to come?

fr.L: Son amour loyal a-t-il cessé pour toujours ? \q [Sa] parole a-t-elle pris fin pour génération après génération ?
fr.B: Son amour fidèle a-t-il disparu pour de bon ? \q Sa promesse est-elle finie pour toutes les générations à venir ?
fr.R: Son amour fidèle est-il fini pour de bon ? \q Ses promesses sont-elles terminées pour toujours ?

sw.L: Je, upendo {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} usiokoma umekoma milele? \q Je, neno [{{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}] limefikia mwisho kwa kizazi baada ya kizazi?
sw.B: Je, upendo {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} usiokoma umetoweka kabisa? \q Je, ahadi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} imekwisha kwa vizazi vyote vijavyo?
sw.R: Je, upendo {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} usiokoma umekwisha kabisa? \q Je, ahadi {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} zimekwisha kwa wakati wote ujao?

decisions.choice: loyal love: God's faithful covenant love
decisions.reason: The word (chesed) is the loyal, faithful love God has bound himself to show his people (5:8). Literal and Balanced say "loyal love", Readable "faithful love".

decisions.choice: word: a promise
decisions.reason: The word ('omer) is a spoken word; here God's word of promise to his people.

decisions.choice: promise
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what kind of word is meant (m2).

source.text: הֲשָׁכַ֣ח חַנּ֣וֹת אֵ֑ל אִם־קָפַ֥ץ בְּ֝אַ֗ף רַחֲמָ֥יו סֶֽלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: Has forgotten to be gracious God, or has he shut up in anger his compassion? Selah.

en.L: Has God forgotten to be gracious? \q Or has {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} shut up {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} compassion in anger? Selah
en.B: Has God forgotten how to show mercy? \q Has {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} let anger lock away {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} compassion? Selah
en.R: Has God forgotten to be kind? \q Is {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} so angry that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will no longer show {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} tender love? Selah

fr.L: Dieu a-t-il oublié de faire grâce ? \q Ou a-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} enfermé {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} compassion dans la colère ? Sélah
fr.B: Dieu a-t-il oublié d’avoir pitié ? \q A-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} laissé la colère enfermer {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} tendresse ? Sélah
fr.R: Dieu a-t-il oublié d’être bon ? \q Est-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} tellement en colère qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne montrera plus {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} amour plein de tendresse ? Sélah

sw.L: Je, Mungu amesahau kuwa na neema? \q Au amezifunga huruma {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} kwa hasira? Sela
sw.B: Je, Mungu amesahau jinsi ya kuonyesha rehema? \q Je, hasira imezifungia mbali huruma {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}? Sela
sw.R: Je, Mungu amesahau kuwa mwema? \q Je, amekasirika sana hata hataonyesha tena upendo {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wa huruma? Sela

decisions.choice: gracious and compassionate: God's own description
decisions.reason: The words echo God's description of himself to Moses as compassionate and gracious (Exodus 34:6). The psalmist asks whether God has forgotten his own character.

decisions.choice: shut up his compassion: hold it back
decisions.reason: The verb (qafats) means to close, as a hand is closed (Deuteronomy 15:7). Anger seems to have closed God's hand of compassion.

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

source.text: וָ֭אֹמַר חַלּ֣וֹתִי הִ֑יא שְׁ֝נ֗וֹת יְמִ֣ין עֶלְיֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And I said: My wounding it [is], [the] changing of [the] right hand of [the] Most High.

en.L: And I said: It is my wound, \q the changing of the right hand of the Most High.
en.B: Then I said: This is what pierces me, \q that the Most High's right hand is not what it was.
en.R: Then I said: What hurts me most is this. \q The God who is above all no longer uses {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power for us as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} once did.

fr.L: Et j’ai dit : C’est ma blessure, \q le changement de la droite du Très-Haut.
fr.B: Alors j’ai dit : Voici ce qui me transperce : \q la main droite du Très-Haut n’est plus ce qu’elle était.
fr.R: Alors j’ai dit : Voici ce qui me fait le plus mal. \q Le Dieu qui est au-dessus de tout n’utilise plus {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} puissance pour nous comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} le faisait avant.

sw.L: Nami nikasema: Hili ni jeraha langu, \q kubadilika kwa mkono wa kuume wa Aliye Juu.
sw.B: Kisha nikasema: Hiki ndicho kinachonichoma, \q kwamba mkono wa kuume wa Aliye Juu si kama ulivyokuwa.
sw.R: Kisha nikasema: Kinachoniumiza zaidi ni hiki. \q Mungu aliye juu ya wote hatumii tena nguvu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} kwa ajili yetu kama alivyofanya zamani.

decisions.choice: my wounding: what hurts me
decisions.reason: The word (challoti) is taken as "my wound" or "my sickness", from chalal or chalah. It may also come from a verb meaning to entreat: "this is my plea".

decisions.choice: changing: the right hand has changed
alternatives: the years of the right hand of the Most High
decisions.reason: The word (shenot) is read as "changing": what hurts is that God's power no longer acts as before. The same letters can mean "years", giving "(I will remember) the years of the right hand of the Most High", which leads into verse 12. The verse is hard and both readings are old.

decisions.choice: the right hand: power to act and rescue
decisions.reason: God's right hand is his power at work for his people, as at the sea (Exodus 15:6, 12). "Most High" ('Elyon) names God as highest over all (46:5).

decisions.choice: The God who is above all no longer uses his power for us as he once did
alternatives: the changing of the right hand of the Most High
decisions.reason: Readable says what the pictures mean (m2, m3) and supplies "for us".

source.text: אֶזְכּ֥וֹר מַֽעַלְלֵי־יָ֑הּ כִּֽי־אֶזְכְּרָ֖ה מִקֶּ֣דֶם פִּלְאֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: I will remember [the] deeds of Yah; for I will remember from antiquity your wonder.

en.L: I will remember the deeds of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}; \q yes, I will remember {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wonders of old.
en.B: I will call to mind what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}} has done; \q yes, I will remember the marvels {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} worked long ago.
en.R: I will remember what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}} has done. \q Yes, I will remember the amazing things {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did long ago.

fr.L: Je me souviendrai des œuvres {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yah}} ; \q oui, je me souviendrai de {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} merveilles d’autrefois.
fr.B: Je rappellerai ce qu’a fait {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yah}} ; \q oui, je me souviendrai des merveilles que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as accomplies jadis.
fr.R: Je me souviendrai de ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yah}} a fait. \q Oui, je me souviendrai des choses étonnantes que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as faites il y a longtemps.

sw.L: Nitayakumbuka matendo ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yah}}; \q naam, nitayakumbuka maajabu {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} ya kale.
sw.B: Nitayakumbuka aliyoyatenda {{divine_name:BWANA|Yah}}; \q naam, nitayakumbuka maajabu uliyoyafanya {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} zamani.
sw.R: Nitakumbuka aliyoyatenda {{divine_name:BWANA|Yah}}. \q Naam, nitakumbuka mambo ya ajabu uliyoyafanya {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} zamani.

decisions.choice: I will remember: the form as read
decisions.reason: The Hebrew writes a form meaning "I will make mention of" (azkir), and its notes say to read "I will remember" (ezkor), as in the next line. The words follow the form to be read.

decisions.choice: Yah: the short form of the divine name
decisions.reason: Yah is the short form of the name YHWH, as in Exodus 15:2 and in "Hallelu-yah".

decisions.choice: your wonder: the psalmist turns to God
decisions.reason: In the middle of the verse the psalmist stops speaking about God and speaks to him. From here to the end of the psalm God is "you". "Wonder" is singular, God's wonderful work as a whole.

decisions.choice: Yah, the short form of the name, is "le SEIGNEUR" by default with "Yah" as the reader's alternative
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets: the default is the same as for the full name, and the alternative shows the short form the Hebrew has here (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: "BWANA" for the short name Yah, with "Yah" as the setting alternative
decisions.reason: The terms note writes the short form of the name with the language's form of "the LORD" by default and "Yah" itself as the alternative, as the English does.

source.text: וְהָגִ֥יתִי בְכָל־פָּעֳלֶ֑ךָ וּֽבַעֲלִ֖ילוֹתֶ֣יךָ אָשִֽׂיחָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will meditate on all your work, and on your deeds I will muse.

en.L: And I will meditate on all {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} work, \q and on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} deeds I will muse.
en.B: I will reflect on all {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} work \q and turn over in my mind what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done.
en.R: I will think about everything {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done \q and go over {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} mighty acts in my mind.

fr.L: Et je méditerai sur toute {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} œuvre, \q et sur {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} actions je réfléchirai.
fr.B: Je méditerai sur toute {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} œuvre \q et je repasserai dans mon esprit ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as fait.
fr.R: Je penserai à tout ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as fait \q et je repasserai dans ma tête {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} grandes actions.

sw.L: Nami nitazitafakari kazi {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} zote, \q na matendo {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} nitayawaza.
sw.B: Nitaitafakari kazi {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} yote \q na kuwaza moyoni yale uliyoyatenda {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}.
sw.R: Nitafikiri juu ya yote uliyoyatenda {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} \q na kuyawaza matendo {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} makuu moyoni.

decisions.choice: meditate: murmur over
decisions.reason: The verb (hagah) means to murmur or say over quietly, as in 1:2. The same musing that weighed him down (verse 4) is now fixed on what God has done.

source.text: אֱ֭לֹהִים בַּקֹּ֣דֶשׁ דַּרְכֶּ֑ךָ מִי־אֵ֥ל גָּ֝ד֗וֹל כֵּֽאלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: God, in holiness [is] your way; who [is] a god great like God?

en.L: God, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} way [is] in holiness; \q who [is] a great god like God?
en.B: God, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} way is holy. \q Is there a god anywhere as great as God?
en.R: God, everything {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do is holy. \q No other god is as great as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are.

fr.L: Ô Dieu, {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} chemin [est] dans la sainteté ; \q quel dieu [est] grand comme Dieu ?
fr.B: Ô Dieu, {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} chemin est saint. \q Existe-t-il un dieu aussi grand que Dieu ?
fr.R: Dieu, tout ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} fais est saint. \q Aucun autre dieu n’est aussi grand que {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}.

sw.L: Ee Mungu, njia {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} [i] katika utakatifu; \q ni mungu gani [aliye] mkuu kama Mungu?
sw.B: Ee Mungu, njia {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} ni takatifu. \q Je, yuko mungu yeyote aliye mkuu kama Mungu?
sw.R: Mungu, kila kitu unachotenda {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni kitakatifu. \q Hakuna mungu mwingine aliye mkuu kama {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}.

decisions.choice: in holiness: holy
decisions.reason: The phrase (baqqodesh) can mean "in holiness" or "in the holy place", as in 68:25. Here it is taken as describing God's way: all he does is holy.

decisions.choice: who is a god like God: the song at the sea
decisions.reason: The question echoes the song Israel sang after crossing the sea: "Who is like you among the gods, LORD, majestic in holiness?" (Exodus 15:11).

decisions.choice: No other god is as great as you are
alternatives: what god is great like God?
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into the statement it implies.

source.text: אַתָּ֣ה הָ֭אֵל עֹ֣שֵׂה פֶ֑לֶא הוֹדַ֖עְתָּ בָעַמִּ֣ים עֻזֶּֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: You [are] the God doing wonder; you made known among the peoples your strength.

en.L: You [are] the God who does wonders; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made known {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} strength among the peoples.
en.B: You are the God whose deeds are marvels; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have shown the nations how strong {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are.
en.R: You are the God who does amazing things. \q You have shown all nations how powerful {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are.

fr.L: Toi, [{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es] le Dieu qui fait des merveilles ; \q {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as fait connaître {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} force parmi les peuples.
fr.B: Tu es le Dieu dont les œuvres sont des merveilles ; \q {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as montré aux peuples combien {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es fort.
fr.R: Tu es le Dieu qui fait des choses étonnantes. \q Tu as montré à tous les peuples combien {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es puissant.

sw.L: Wewe [ndiwe] Mungu atendaye maajabu; \q {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} umezijulisha nguvu {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} kati ya mataifa.
sw.B: Wewe ndiwe Mungu ambaye matendo {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} ni ya ajabu; \q {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} umeyaonyesha mataifa jinsi ulivyo na nguvu.
sw.R: Wewe ndiwe Mungu atendaye mambo ya ajabu. \q Umeyaonyesha mataifa yote jinsi ulivyo na uweza.

decisions.choice: doing wonders: as at the sea
decisions.reason: The song at the sea calls God the one "doing wonders" (Exodus 15:11), and says the peoples heard and trembled (Exodus 15:14).

decisions.choice: the peoples: the nations
decisions.reason: God's rescue of Israel showed his strength to the other nations as well.

source.text: גָּאַ֣לְתָּ בִּזְר֣וֹעַ עַמֶּ֑ךָ בְּנֵי־יַעֲקֹ֖ב וְיוֹסֵ֣ף סֶֽלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: You redeemed with an arm your people, [the] sons of Jacob and Joseph. Selah.

en.L: You redeemed {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people with [{{deity_pronoun:your|Your}}] arm, \q the sons of Jacob and Joseph. Selah
en.B: With {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} strong arm {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} set {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people free, \q the families of Jacob and Joseph. Selah
en.R: You used {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great power to rescue {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, \q the families of Jacob and Joseph. Selah

fr.L: Tu as racheté {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} peuple par [{{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}}] bras, \q les fils de Jacob et de Joseph. Sélah
fr.B: Par {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} bras puissant {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as libéré {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} peuple, \q les descendants de Jacob et de Joseph. Sélah
fr.R: Tu as utilisé {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} grande puissance pour délivrer {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} peuple, \q les familles de Jacob et de Joseph. Sélah

sw.L: Wewe uliwakomboa watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} kwa mkono [{{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}], \q wana wa Yakobo na Yusufu. Sela
sw.B: Kwa mkono {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wenye nguvu {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} uliwaweka huru watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, \q jamaa za Yakobo na Yusufu. Sela
sw.R: Ulitumia uweza {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} mkuu kuwaokoa watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, \q jamaa za Yakobo na Yusufu. Sela

decisions.choice: redeemed with an arm: the exodus
decisions.reason: God promised to redeem Israel "with an outstretched arm" (Exodus 6:6), and the song at the sea praises the people he redeemed (Exodus 15:13, 16).

decisions.choice: Jacob and Joseph: all Israel
decisions.reason: Jacob is the father of all the tribes; Joseph, the father of Ephraim and Manasseh, stands for the northern tribes and recalls the years in Egypt. Together they name the whole people.

decisions.choice: strong arm (B); great power (R)
decisions.reason: An arm is a picture of strength in action; Balanced adds "strong" and Readable says "power".

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

source.text: רָ֘א֤וּךָ מַּ֨יִם׀אֱֽלֹהִ֗ים רָא֣וּךָ מַּ֣יִם יָחִ֑ילוּ אַ֝֗ף יִרְגְּז֥וּ תְהֹמֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: They saw you, [the] waters, God; they saw you, [the] waters; they writhed; even trembled [the] deeps.

en.L: The waters saw {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, God; \q the waters saw {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [and] writhed; \q even the deeps trembled.
en.B: God, when the waters caught sight of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q when the waters saw {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, they twisted in fear; \q even the deep sea quaked.
en.R: God, when the sea saw {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, it was afraid. \q The waters twisted in pain, \q and even the deepest ocean shook.

fr.L: Les eaux {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}ont vu, ô Dieu ; \q les eaux {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}ont vu [et] se sont tordues ; \q même les abîmes ont tremblé.
fr.B: Ô Dieu, quand les eaux {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}ont aperçu, \q quand les eaux {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}ont vu, elles se sont tordues de peur ; \q même les profondeurs de la mer ont frémi.
fr.R: Dieu, quand la mer {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}a vu, elle a eu peur. \q Les eaux se sont tordues de douleur, \q et même l’océan le plus profond a tremblé.

sw.L: Maji yalikuona {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, Ee Mungu; \q maji yalikuona {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} [na] kugaagaa; \q hata vilindi vilitetemeka.
sw.B: Ee Mungu, maji yalipokuona {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, \q maji yalipokuona {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, yalijikunja kwa hofu; \q hata bahari ya kina ilitetemeka.
sw.R: Mungu, bahari ilipokuona {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, iliogopa. \q Maji yalijikunja kwa maumivu, \q na hata bahari yenye kina kirefu kabisa ilitetemeka.

decisions.choice: the waters saw you: the sea at the exodus
decisions.reason: The psalm now tells the crossing of the sea (Exodus 14:21-22) as God's appearing in a storm. Psalm 114:3 says likewise, "The sea saw and fled".

decisions.choice: writhed: twisted as in pain
decisions.reason: The verb (chil) is used of a woman in labor (48:7). The sea is pictured as a living thing in anguish before God.

decisions.choice: the deeps: the depths of the waters
decisions.reason: The deeps (tehomot) are the great waters below (Genesis 1:2), which at the sea "congealed" before God (Exodus 15:8).

source.text: זֹ֤רְמוּ מַ֨יִם׀עָב֗וֹת ק֭וֹלנָתְנ֣וּ שְׁחָקִ֑ים אַף־חֲ֝צָצֶ֗יךָ יִתְהַלָּֽכוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Poured out water [the] clouds; a sound gave [the] skies; also your arrows went about.

en.L: The clouds poured out water; \q the skies gave forth a sound; \q also {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} arrows went back and forth.
en.B: The clouds poured down rain, \q the skies rumbled with thunder, \q and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} arrows flashed this way and that.
en.R: The clouds poured down rain. \q Thunder crashed in the sky. \q Your lightning shot out like arrows in every direction.

fr.L: Les nuées ont déversé de l’eau ; \q les cieux ont fait entendre une voix ; \q {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} flèches aussi allaient de-ci de-là.
fr.B: Les nuages ont versé la pluie, \q le ciel a grondé de tonnerre, \q et {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} flèches jaillissaient de tous côtés.
fr.R: Les nuages ont versé la pluie. \q Le tonnerre a éclaté dans le ciel. \q Tes éclairs partaient comme des flèches dans toutes les directions.

sw.L: Mawingu yalimwaga maji; \q anga zilitoa sauti; \q nayo mishale {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} ilienda huku na huko.
sw.B: Mawingu yalimimina mvua, \q anga zilinguruma kwa radi, \q na mishale {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} ilimulika huku na huko.
sw.R: Mawingu yalimimina mvua. \q Radi ilipasuka angani. \q Umeme {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} ulifyatuka kama mishale pande zote.

decisions.choice: your arrows: lightning
decisions.reason: The arrows are bolts of lightning, as in 18:15 and 144:6, God's weapons in the storm.

decisions.choice: a sound: thunder
decisions.reason: The word (qol), "voice" or "sound", is used for thunder (29:3).

decisions.choice: Your lightning shot out like arrows
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means (m1) and keeps it as a comparison.

source.text: ק֤וֹל רַעַמְךָ֨׀בַּגַּלְגַּ֗ל הֵאִ֣ירוּ בְרָקִ֣ים תֵּבֵ֑ל רָגְזָ֖ה וַתִּרְעַ֣שׁ הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] sound of your thunder [was] in the whirlwind; lightnings lit up [the] world; trembled and shook the earth.

en.L: The sound of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} thunder [was] in the whirlwind; \q lightnings lit up the world; \q the earth trembled and shook.
en.B: Your thunder rumbled in the whirlwind; \q flashes of lightning lit the world; \q the earth shook and quaked.
en.R: Your thunder roared in the storm. \q Lightning lit up the whole world. \q The ground shook and trembled.

fr.L: La voix de {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} tonnerre [était] dans le tourbillon ; \q les éclairs ont illuminé le monde ; \q la terre a tremblé et s’est ébranlée.
fr.B: Ton tonnerre a grondé dans le tourbillon ; \q les éclairs ont illuminé le monde ; \q la terre a frémi et tremblé.
fr.R: Ton tonnerre a rugi dans la tempête. \q Les éclairs ont éclairé le monde entier. \q Le sol a bougé et tremblé.

sw.L: Sauti ya radi {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} [ilikuwa] katika kisulisuli; \q umeme uliuangaza ulimwengu; \q nchi ilitetemeka na kutikisika.
sw.B: Radi {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} ilivuma katika kisulisuli; \q miali ya umeme iliuangaza ulimwengu; \q nchi ilitikisika na kutetemeka.
sw.R: Radi {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} ilinguruma katika dhoruba. \q Umeme uliuangaza ulimwengu wote. \q Ardhi ilitikisika na kutetemeka.

decisions.choice: the whirlwind: the swirling storm
decisions.reason: The word (galgal) means a wheel or something that whirls. It may be the storm wind, or the wheels of God's chariot as he rides through the sky (Ezekiel 10:13).

decisions.choice: thunder, lightning, quaking: God's coming
decisions.reason: Thunder, lightning and a shaking earth mark God's coming at Sinai (Exodus 19:16-18) and in 18:8-16. Exodus 14:24 tells that he looked down on the Egyptian army from the pillar of fire and cloud.

source.text: בַּיָּ֤ם דַּרְכֶּ֗ךָ וּֽ֭שְׁבִֽילְךָ בְּמַ֣יִם רַבִּ֑ים וְ֝עִקְּבוֹתֶ֗יךָ לֹ֣א נֹדָֽעוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: In the sea [was] your way, and your path in waters many, and your footprints not were known.

en.L: Your way [was] in the sea, \q and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} path in many waters, \q and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} footprints were not known.
en.B: Your road went through the sea \q and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} track through the deep waters, \q but no trace of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} steps could be seen.
en.R: You made a road through the sea \q and a path through the deep water. \q But no one could see {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} footprints.

fr.L: Ton chemin [était] dans la mer, \q et {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} sentier dans les grandes eaux, \q et {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} traces n’ont pas été connues.
fr.B: Ta route passait par la mer, \q et {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} sentier par les eaux profondes, \q mais on ne pouvait voir aucune trace de {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} pas.
fr.R: Tu as fait une route à travers la mer \q et un chemin à travers l’eau profonde. \q Mais personne ne pouvait voir {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} traces de pas.

sw.L: Njia {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} [ilikuwa] baharini, \q na mapito {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} katika maji mengi, \q na nyayo {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} hazikujulikana.
sw.B: Barabara {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} ilipita katikati ya bahari \q na mapito {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} katika maji ya kina, \q lakini alama ya hatua {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} haikuonekana.
sw.R: Ulitengeneza barabara katikati ya bahari \q na njia katikati ya maji ya kina. \q Lakini hakuna aliyeweza kuziona nyayo {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}}.

decisions.choice: your path: the form as read
decisions.reason: The Hebrew writes "your paths" and its notes say to read "your path", matching "your way". The words follow the form to be read.

decisions.choice: your way in the sea: the crossing
decisions.reason: God made a way through the sea for Israel (Exodus 14:21-22, 29; Isaiah 43:16).

decisions.choice: your footprints not known: God unseen, yet at work
decisions.reason: No one saw God's footsteps; the waters closed behind him. He was present and acting though unseen, and he led his people through human leaders (verse 21).

source.text: נָחִ֣יתָ כַצֹּ֣אן עַמֶּ֑ךָ בְּֽיַד־מֹשֶׁ֥ה וְאַהֲרֹֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: You led like the flock your people by [the] hand of Moses and Aaron.

en.L: You led {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people like a flock \q by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
en.B: Like a shepherd with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sheep {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} guided {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, \q through Moses and Aaron.
en.R: You led {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people as a shepherd leads sheep, \q and Moses and Aaron were the ones who guided them.

fr.L: Tu as conduit {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} peuple comme un troupeau \q par la main de Moïse et d’Aaron.
fr.B: Comme un berger mène ses brebis, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as guidé {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} peuple \q par Moïse et Aaron.
fr.R: Tu as conduit {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} peuple comme un berger conduit ses moutons, \q et Moïse et Aaron étaient ceux qui le guidaient.

sw.L: Uliwaongoza watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} kama kundi \q kwa mkono wa Musa na Haruni.
sw.B: Kama mchungaji na kondoo wake, uliwaongoza watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} \q kupitia Musa na Haruni.
sw.R: Uliwaongoza watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} kama mchungaji anavyowaongoza kondoo, \q na Musa na Haruni ndio waliowaongoza.

decisions.choice: by the hand of: through
decisions.reason: "By the hand of" means "through" someone as God's agent. God himself led, but his leading was done through Moses and Aaron (Numbers 33:1).

decisions.choice: like a flock: God as shepherd
decisions.reason: The picture of God as shepherd of his people (23:2; 80:2) closes the psalm without a return to the lament. Psalm 78 takes up the same picture (78:52, 70-72).

decisions.choice: Like a shepherd with his sheep (B); as a shepherd leads sheep (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out the shepherd the picture implies (m2).
